prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1424; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. The policyholder is the named driver, and police confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Scene photos and statements from two independent witnesses line up with the claimant's description of the impact, and the other driver's account matches. The vehicle damage is largely in line with the reported force of the collision.

Entry 3: The claimant reports headaches, dizziness and sensitivity to light after the crash and was diagnosed with a concussion at urgent care. The injury pattern appears consistent with the kind and force of this impact.

Entry 4: Records show prior treatment for the same body area within the past two years, and that earlier condition appears to add to the current complaints. This has been noted for the file and will be weighed when the bodily injury portion is evaluated.

Entry 5: The claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation so far, including the initial call, the recorded statement and the follow-up with counsel present. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 6: Treatment has followed a usual course with regular follow-up visits, and symptoms have tapered as the patient has improved. The most recent medical notes reflect steady progress.

Entry 7: The repair estimate was reviewed against the photos. The named driver is confirmed on the policy, and coverage was verified as in force at the time of loss.

Entry 8: File reviewed with the adjuster supervisor. The claim remains open pending final medical updates and the attorney's demand package.
